newsitem.title: USA: CSCE world sugar called to open 0.05 cent higher.
newsitem.headline: CSCE world sugar called to open 0.05 cent higher.

text.p: CSCE world sugar was called to open 0.05 cent a lb firmer on Thursday on follow-through buying from the previous session, dealers said.

Wednesday, the benchmark October contract rose to 11.34 cents, its highest level since reaching 11.40 cents on July 1, amid chart-drive fund buying. Several of the back months surged to new life-of-contract highs before easing slightly ahead of the close.
October ended 0.33 cent higher at 11.30 cents, while the rest of the board finished 0.31 to 0.15 cent firmer.
An estimated 33,951 lots changed hands on the day.
The October contract is expected to test resistance at 11.35 followed by 11.40 cents, dealers said.
Mexico said late Monday its 1996/97 sugar crop could reach a record 4.544 million tonnes. Output reached 4.378 million tonnes last season, the National Sugar Chamber said.
LIFFE white sugar futures were trading higher on Thursday following the expiry of the August contract. At 0848 EDT/1248 GMT, LIFFE October stood $1.20 firmer at $324.00.
